field_decisions.assigned_value: SB 197 is the state government agencies budget/appropriations vehicle bill ('AN ACT providing funding and establishing conditions for state government agencies and institutions, making an appropriation therefor, and declaring an emergency'), not a standalone data-center policy bill. House Committee Substitute 1 (2026-03-27) inserted HB 593-style data center electric-service provisions for municipal electric utilities: application/tariff process, $75,000 minimum nonrefundable application fee, 25 MW dedicated-resource threshold, prohibition on subsidizing data center customers via non-data-center rates, and curtailment-allocation rules. That language does not appear in House Committee Substitute 2 (2026-04-15), the version that actually passed both chambers, or in the final enacted bill text. SB 197 was enacted as Acts Ch. 202 (with Governor line-item vetoes of unrelated appropriations items) but contains no data center provisions in its final form.

field_decisions.proposed_value: SB 197 originated as a county-tiered economic-development incentives bill and became a supplemental appropriations vehicle. HCS1, reported March 27, proposed data-center electric-service rules for municipal utilities and retail suppliers, including contracts, tariffs, cost allocation and curtailment; for municipal utilities the application included an initial nonrefundable fee of at least $75,000 and information on a proposed dedicated resource when contract capacity exceeds 25 MW. HCS2 passed both chambers April 15; neither its retained text nor the enrolled text contains a 'data center' text match. The retained comparison does not determine whether similar rules became law elsewhere.
